result.abstractText:
Background and aims

Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) detection is crucial for improving survival. While narrow-band imaging (NBI) improves mucosal visualization, limitations remain. We evaluated the diagnostic performance of the Spectrum-Aided Vision Enhancer (SAVE), an algorithmic NBI-like technology reconstructed from white light imaging (WLI).

Methods

We conducted a retrospective, image-based exploratory feasibility study to descriptively evaluate the diagnostic performance of WLI, NBI, and SAVE. A dataset of 1350 still endoscopic images (450 each for WLI, NBI, and SAVE) across normal mucosa, dysplasia, and ESCC stages from 158 patients was blindly reviewed by three endoscopists with different experience levels (3, 5, and 15 years). Diagnostic metrics included sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, and reading time.

Results

For ESCC, SAVE demonstrated diagnostic performance metrics (sensitivity: 0.81-0.97, specificity: 0.85-0.96) that were numerically similar to WLI and NBI. For dysplasia detection, SAVE had lower observed sensitivity (0.39-0.62) compared to NBI (0.55-0.85) across all observers, representing a clinical limitation for precancerous screening in its current format. Mean per-image reading times were similar across WLI, NBI, and SAVE.

Conclusions

In this retrospective study, SAVE showed diagnostic potential for ESCC, with observed diagnostic performance metrics numerically similar to those of WLI and NBI in this exploratory dataset, but lacked sensitivity for dysplasia. These findings are hypothesis-generating and warrant further prospective, multicenter validation to refine the algorithm for early cancer detection.

result.abstractText: Endoscopic subepithelial dissection is a minimally invasive treatment for superficial pharyngeal neoplastic lesions, requiring preservation of important neural structures such as the internal branch of the superior laryngeal nerve (ibSLN). We report a case in which red dichromatic imaging (RDI) appeared to improve the visualization of a linear structure presumed to be the ibSLN compared with white-light imaging (WLI). A 57-year-old woman underwent endoscopic subepithelial dissection for a 5-mm superficial lesion on the pharyngoepiglottic fold. Both WLI and RDI revealed a whitish linear structure beneath the lesion, which was presumed to represent the ibSLN based on its anatomical location and course. The presumed nerve structure appeared to be more clearly delineated with RDI than with WLI before mucosal incision and remained identifiable after submucosal injection and during dissection. This enhanced visualization may have helped guide the selection of the mucosal incision line and dissection plane. En bloc resection was achieved without apparent nerve injury. No dysphagia, hoarseness, or other adverse events occurred postoperatively. These findings suggest that RDI may serve as a useful adjunct for visualization of the structure presumed to represent the ibSLN during pharyngeal endoscopic subepithelial dissection and may support nerve-preserving strategies.

result.abstractText:
Background

Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is common in type 2 diabetes. We investigated the association between monocyte mRNA expression of sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2), the molecular target of luseogliflozin, and changes in the fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) index during treatment with this agent.

Methods

This single-center retrospective observational study used prospectively collected peripheral blood monocyte samples from 82 participants with type 2 diabetes and MASLD who had received luseogliflozin for at least 6 months. Baseline monocyte SGLT2 mRNA expression was measured using quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction. Clinical and laboratory parameters, including FIB-4 index, were evaluated at baseline and 6 months after luseogliflozin initiation. Changes were calculated as the 6-month value minus the baseline value; therefore, negative values indicated reductions.

Results

After 6 months, waist circumference, hemoglobin A1c, liver enzyme levels, high-sensitivity C-reactive protein, and the FIB-4 index decreased significantly. Baseline monocyte SGLT2 mRNA expression was negatively correlated with the change in the FIB-4 index, indicating that higher baseline expression was associated with a greater reduction. In multiple regression analyses, natural-log-transformed baseline monocyte SGLT2 mRNA expression remained associated with the change in the FIB-4 index after adjustment for baseline clinical variables.

Conclusions

Higher baseline monocyte SGLT2 mRNA expression was associated with a greater reduction in the FIB-4 index after luseogliflozin treatment. This finding should be interpreted as an exploratory association between a cell-specific transcriptomic feature and changes in a fibrosis-related index, rather than as evidence of functional SGLT2 signaling in monocytes or histological fibrosis regression.

result.abstractText: This review examines the current literature on the application of atomic force microscopy (AFM) to cancer mechanophenotyping, with particular emphasis on cellular Young's modulus and its potential diagnostic significance. A structured electronic search of PubMed, Scopus and Google Scholar was conducted to identify studies published between 1999 and 2025 reporting AFM-based measurements of cellular Young's modulus in cancer-related models. Across multiple malignancies, reduced cellular stiffness is frequently observed in malignant compared with non-malignant cells and is associated with cytoskeletal remodelling, increased deformability and altered cell-matrix interactions. However, the relationship between Young's modulus and malignancy is not universally monotonic. Nanomechanical properties may vary across different pathological states and malignant phenotypes rather than following a simple monotonic trajectory, while invasive and metastatic cells can dynamically remodel their cytoskeleton and modify their stiffness in response to environmental and mechanical constraints. Young's modulus should therefore not be regarded as an isolated universal cancer biomarker, but rather as one component of a dynamic mechanophenotype influenced by disease stage, cellular region, microenvironment and measurement methodology. Recent advances in automated force acquisition, optical cell recognition, artificial intelligence and high-throughput AFM are beginning to address traditional limitations in measurement efficiency and operator dependence. The future diagnostic value of AFM may therefore lie in integrating Young's modulus with complementary parameters, including spatial mechanical heterogeneity, viscoelasticity, adhesion, deformation-energy characteristics and nanotopography, to define multidimensional cancer mechanophenotypes. Standardised acquisition and analysis protocols, together with validation in patient-derived specimens, will be essential for translating AFM nanomechanics from an experimental measurement into a clinically informative biomechanical biomarker.

result.abstractText: Intestinal dysbiosis is a hallmark of alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD) characterized by a higher abundance of unfavorable species and a reduction of beneficial species. In this study, we aimed to analyze the bacterial proteome of stool samples from patients with alcohol-associated hepatitis (AH) (n = 80), alcohol use disorder (AUD; n = 20), and controls (n = 19) from an international multicenter cohort using quantitative tandem mass tag (TMT)-based metaproteomic profiling. We validated our results in an independent multicenter cohort of 72 patients with AH at the genomic level using qPCR. We detected 2,364 bacterial proteins and identified distinct metaproteomic signatures separating controls, patients with AUD, and AH. Patients with AUD and AH were characterized by depletion of Firmicutes-derived proteins and enrichment of proteins from Bacteroidetes, Proteobacteria, and Actinobacteria. Eighteen bacterial proteins increased with disease severity, many with multifunctional "moonlighting" roles, including enolase and hexokinase. DUF6383 domain-containing protein from Parabacteroides distasonis is correlated with histological injury, inflammatory cell infiltration, and is linked to neutrophil degranulation in the host. Patients with a high abundance of DUF6383 domain-containing protein had significantly lower 90-day survival, and this association was validated by qPCR at the genomic level in a second cohort. Our findings show that microbial proteins are associated with disease severity and progression, and that DUF6383 domain-containing protein from P. distasonis is a potential prognostic biomarker for AH.

result.abstractText:
Objectives

The environmental impact of endoscopic techniques remains poorly defined. We compared procedure-related environmental outcomes between conventional endoscopic mucosal resection (EMR) and underwater EMR (U-EMR) for colorectal lesions.

Methods

In this prospective pilot procedure-based life cycle assessment of the resection phase, 10-25-mm colorectal lesions underwent EMR or U-EMR across three endoscopy units. Outcomes included global warming potential (GWP, kg CO2-equivalent/procedure), waste, life-cycle water consumption, fossil resource scarcity, and terrestrial acidification. Exploratory GWP per en bloc resection was estimated using pooled randomized-trial and pilot-cohort data.

Results

Forty-nine procedures were included: 23 EMR and 26 U-EMR. En bloc resection was achieved in 56.5% of EMR and 69.2% of U-EMR, and R0 resection in 52.2% and 69.2%. Mean GWP was significantly lower with U-EMR than EMR (1.92 ± 0.54 vs. 2.42 ± 0.50 kg CO2-eq; p = 0.002), corresponding to a reduction of 0.50 kg CO2-eq per procedure and 50 kg CO2-eq per 100 procedures. U-EMR was associated with lower waste generation (324.0 ± 78.3 vs. 407.3 ± 72.0 g; p < 0.001), water consumption (0.56 ± 0.17 vs. 0.77 ± 0.20 m3; p < 0.001), fossil resource scarcity (0.33 ± 0.10 vs. 0.40 ± 0.09 kg oil-eq; p = 0.007), and terrestrial acidification (0.0052 ± 0.0018 vs. 0.0068 ± 0.0018 kg SO2-eq; p = 0.003). Findings were consistent across scenario and uncertainty analyses. In the meta-analysis-based model, GWP per en bloc resection was lower with U-EMR than EMR (2.59 vs. 3.51 kg CO2-eq), corresponding to a 26.3% relative reduction.

Conclusions

U-EMR was associated with lower procedure-related environmental burden than conventional EMR, persisting after normalization for en bloc resection.

result.abstractText:
Objectives

Non-ampullary duodenal epithelial tumors differ in clinicopathological features according to mucin phenotype. Gastric-type tumors have distinct biological features; however, their associated mucosal background remains unclear. In this study, gastric foveolar metaplasia, gastric heterotopia, and Brunner's gland hyperplasia were collectively referred to as gastric-type mucosal lesions (G-MLs). We aimed to assess their prevalence and associations with mucin phenotype and clinicopathological factors.

Methods

We retrospectively analyzed the data of 130 patients with 130 resected non-ampullary duodenal epithelial tumors at a single center. Tumors were classified according to mucin phenotype. The prevalence of concomitant G-MLs and associated factors was evaluated. Exploratory Firth-penalized logistic regression analysis was used to assess the association between gastric-type tumors and G-ML presence.

Results

Concomitant G-MLs were identified in 44 patients (33.8%). Their prevalence was higher in gastric-type tumors (13/16; 81.3%) than in gastric-intestinal-type tumors (10/37; 27.0%) and intestinal-type tumors (21/77; 27.3%). G-MLs were associated with mild endoscopic gastric mucosal atrophy and smoking status and were inversely associated with current Helicobacter pylori infection. In the exploratory fully adjusted model, gastric-type tumors remained positively associated with the presence of G-MLs (adjusted odds ratio, 7.00; 95% confidence interval, 1.98-30.95; p = 0.002).

Conclusions

G-MLs were present in approximately one-third of patients and were most frequent in gastric-type tumors. These findings indicate an association between G-MLs and gastric-type tumors; however, the cross-sectional design does not allow inference of a biological relationship.

result.abstractText: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD) represents a leading cause of chronic low back pain worldwide, imposing considerable public health and socioeconomic burdens. Current clinical interventions remain largely palliative, unable to reverse the progressive pathological cascade. This cascade is driven by a core self-amplifying triad of oxidative stress, chronic inflammation, and nutrient deprivation within the unique avascular, high-load disc niche, and ultimately progresses to end-stage terminal phenotypes such as biomechanical failure and neurovascular ingrowth. Over recent years, biomaterial-based regenerative strategies have evolved from passive structural fillers toward multifunctional platforms capable of active microenvironmental reprogramming. This review provides a systematic, critical synthesis of state-of-the-art advances in the field, organized within a hierarchical framework spanning immunometabolic modulation of the degenerative niche and targeted delivery of cellular and molecular therapeutics with further elaboration of precision-stratified design and whole-disc tissue engineering. We critically appraise evidence maturity across different strategy classes and dissect disc-specific translational barriers, noting that most candidate platforms remain at preclinical validation stages. Building on this analysis, we outline priority research directions and realistic near-term translational milestones to guide rational development of next-generation regenerative platforms toward durable functional disc repair.

result.abstractText:
Background and objectives

Breast cancer molecular subtype determination is crucial for personalized treatment planning but currently relies on expensive gene expression profiling or immunohistochemistry with discordance rates up to 30%. This study presents a systematic comparison of context-awareness mechanisms for molecular subtype prediction directly from H&E whole-slide images, evaluating graph-based spatial modeling against attention-based aggregation across multiple architectures, datasets, and deployment scenarios.

Methods

The WSI2Graph framework is adapted to represent whole-slide images as spatial KNN graphs, enabling a controlled comparison of context-aware (CA) graph convolutional aggregation against non-context-aware (NCA) attention-based pooling under identical feature extraction. Three evaluation protocols (EP1-EP3) assess within-domain performance (EP1; BCNB dataset, 1058 core-needle biopsies), constrained cross-domain transfer (EP2; SBC dataset, 533 surgical resection specimens), and foundation model integration (EP3; CONCH), all validated with McNemar's paired tests. Graph topology characterization, quantitative interpretability analysis along three axes (attention concentration, tissue composition, spatial coverage), and per-class clinical metrics for therapeutically relevant subtypes are additionally reported.

Results

Within-domain (EP1), CA significantly outperforms NCA on all three classification tasks (p<0.025), with accuracy gains of +4.6, +9.2, and +8.7 percentage points for binary, ternary, and quaternary subtype classification. A capacity and coordinate ablation shows that aggregator capacity accounts for a substantial portion of the observed accuracy advantage, while true spatial coordinates reduce training variance across tasks. Under constrained transfer (EP2), CA matches NCA on binary and quaternary tasks, with only the ternary task showing a significant NCA advantage (p=0.002). With foundation model features (EP3), no significant CA-NCA differences were detected (p>0.07), consistent with feature quality and the broader retraining scope of EP3 outweighing aggregation strategy for cross-domain transfer. Context-aware models significantly outperform attention-based aggregation within-domain, but this advantage does not persist uniformly under domain shift. result.abstractText: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IDD) remains a major cause of chronic low back pain, yet effective disease-modifying therapies are lacking. Current advanced interventions, including cell-based therapies and matrix supplementation, often disrupt disc structural integrity and fail to achieve sustained regeneration. Here, we rationally designed and synthesized a series of arginine-based poly(ester amide)s (Arg-PEAs) as endplate-penetrating biomaterials for non-direct disc therapy. Unlike conventional intradiscal injection, Arg-PEAs were administered into the adjacent vertebral bodies, enabling trans-endplate delivery into the nucleus pulposus (NP). Among them, the lead polymer 8A6S demonstrated excellent biocompatibility and efficient accumulation within the NP, as confirmed by ex vivo and in vivo imaging. Mechanistically, 8A6S suppressed IL-17 signaling by attenuating TRAF6-mediated NF-κB activation, thereby reducing inflammatory catabolism (MMP13, ADAMTS5) and restoring anabolic extracellular matrix markers (ACAN, COL2A1, SOX9). This re-establishment of matrix homeostasis promoted NP regeneration in both rat and caprine models of IDD. Collectively, this study establishes Arg-PEAs as a new class of bioactive polymers capable of trans-endplate delivery and inflammation-modulating regeneration, providing a minimally invasive and structurally preserving strategy for IDD treatment.

Objectives

Sustainable development oals in gastrointestinal endoscopy (GIE), referred to as "green endoscopy," have been a research focus in Western countries. However, the environmental burden of GIE in Japan is poorly understood. We quantify medical waste and estimate GIE-derived incineration-related CO2 emissions in Japan.

Methods

In a dual-center observational study, we report waste from esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD), colonoscopy (CS), endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP), and endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) from June 2024 to January 2025. We classify waste as infectious/non-infectious, combustible/non-combustible, liquid, or sharps. We record the per-procedure waste and the procedure time, estimate CO2 emissions from the combustion of the measured waste mass using combustion equations for cellulose and polyethylene, and calculate per-minute emissions and annual totals. Sensitivity analyses are performed for changes in the anticipated waste composition.

Results

Estimated per-procedure CO2 emissions are 949, 1178, 5834, and 4780 g for EGD, CS, ESD, and ERCP, respectively. Aggregate per-minute emissions are 168, 165, 89, and 75 g/min for ERCP, EGD, CS, and ESD, respectively. Annual institutional emissions total approximately 5800 kg. Estimated emissions are 64%-69% and 123%-134% of the base composition scenario values in the lower- and higher-emission composition scenarios, respectively.

Conclusions

ESD had the highest per-procedure emissions, and ERCP and EGD had the highest per-minute emissions. These results provide preliminary baseline data on incineration-derived CO2 emissions as a foundation for promoting "green endoscopy."

result.abstractText: Engineering multicellular constructs through biophysical cues, independent of soluble biochemical factors, is a promising strategy to boost the therapeutic potential of stem cells for regenerative medicine. However, the mechanisms by which spatially organized cell-cell and cell-matrix interfaces govern multicellular signaling and subsequent behavioral outcomes remain poorly understood. Here, we elucidate these mechanistic events by introducing 2D nanoplates (∼350 nm) compartmentalized within the intercellular space of mesenchymal stem cell (MSC) spheroids to form de novo cell-matrix spatial interfaces. These interfaces redistribute internal stress across the spheroid, amplifying integrin-cytoskeleton-nucleus force transmission and restoring YAP-dependent mechanotransduction to achieve spatial mechanopriming. Cells within these mechanoprimed spheroids exhibit profound nuclear deformation, epigenetic remodeling, and spatially patterned metabolic activation. Finite element modeling and spatial transcriptomic analyses further reveal a spheroid-wide reorganization of cytoskeletal and transcriptional networks. Mechanistically, elevated cytoskeletal tension across the reorganized interfaces is associated with a putative, tension-associated pseudo-hypoxic signature involving HIF-1α-related signaling, establishing a mechanometabolic niche that robustly enhances angiogenic secretion. Consequently, mechanoprimed spheroids demonstrate superior engraftment, accelerated vascular regeneration, and improved perfusion recovery in a murine ischemia model. Collectively, this work establishes spatial mechanopriming as an effective strategy to remodel cytoskeletal-to-nuclear mechanics and enhance the therapeutic potential of 3D multicellular systems.

result.abstractText: Electrospun nanofibers (ESNFs) have become a major focus of modern research given their adaptable architecture, extensive interface, and distinctive physicochemical characteristics, making them appropriate for varied applications such as catalysis and environmental cleanup, drug delivery (DD), tissue engineering (TE), sensing, actuation, and various energy-related technologies. As a result, electrospinning (ES) has emerged as a versatile manufacturing technique, driving intensive efforts to engineer nanofibrous structures specifically for biomedical purposes. Functionalization of ESNFs can be achieved by embedding functional agents or altering surface chemistry to introduce specific functionalities. This review discusses the fabrication methods, optimization techniques, and broad biomedical applications of modified ESNFs, emphasizing their key properties, including biocompatibility, degradability, and safety profile. The article outlines various strategies for creating and modifying ESNFs, followed by a comprehensive analysis of their applications in tissue regeneration, DD, wound repair, antimicrobial therapy, cancer diagnostics and treatment, and biosensing. By critically evaluating recent advances, highlighting future directions, and addressing ongoing challenges about ES, this review underscores the transformative potential of functionalized ESNFs as efficient and adaptable biomaterials for biomedical technologies.

result.abstractText: Partial nephrectomy (PN) is the gold standard for treating renal tumors and trauma; however, massive nephron loss and persistent fibrosis readily lead to chronic kidney disease (CKD). Current therapeutic options remain non-curative and costly, as nearly half of PN patients inevitably progress to end-stage renal failure. Here, we present an innovative regenerative platform for PN-induced CKD, integrating structural biomimicry with targeted molecular inhibition. Harnessing light-based bioprinting of gelatin and hyaluronic acid methacrylates coupled with removable alginate microfiber, we constructed a hierarchical channel scaffold (HCS) that features precisely patterned macrochannels and template-derived microchannels, which closely mimics native kidney architecture, provides structural support, and remarkably enhances cell migration (∼5.45-fold) and rapid neovascularization (∼7.66-fold) over unidirectional channel structures. Moreover, interleukin 11 (IL11) was identified as a novel therapeutic target in kidney fibrosis after PN. Thus, extracellular vesicles (EVs) derived from mesenchymal stem cells loaded with IL11 small interfering RNA (siIL11) were homogeneously encapsulated into HCS, achieving over 4-fold higher renal retention than systemic delivery in PN-induced CKD mice. Furthermore, sustained local release of EV-siIL11 and hierarchically channeled HCS guided synergistic regenerative effects that remarkably inhibited fibrosis, cell cycle arrest, and immune responses, thereby potently preventing kidney atrophy and restoring renal structure with newly aligned nephrons and vasculature, ultimately recovering kidney function. Further analysis revealed that IL11 silencing reversed epithelial‒mesenchymal transition by suppressing the STAT3-ERK-GSK3β-SNAI1 axis. This topological multifunctional hydrogel platform offers a localized, sustained, and clinically translatable strategy for postsurgical kidney regeneration.

result.abstractText: Digital lymphatic anatomy has been defined largely by cadaveric studies. result.abstractText: Psychrotrophic Gram-negative bacteria and thermophilic or thermoduric spore-forming bacteria are major causes of quality deterioration and shelf-life loss in milk and dairy products. Their impact is mediated primarily by heat-stable peptidases and lipases, heat-resistant spores and biofilms that persist in processing environments; with the notable exception of toxigenic members of the Bacillus cereus group, most of these organisms are spoilage rather than safety hazards. Culture-based methods remain the reference standard but are slow and provide single time-point information. This review critically evaluates molecular and sensing methods, including quantitative and digital PCR, isothermal amplification, CRISPR-Cas assays, biosensors, viability assays, spectroscopy and (meta)omics, with explicit attention to whether performance has been demonstrated in naturally contaminated dairy matrices rather than in buffer or spiked samples, and examines how their outputs could inform predictive microbiology and machine learning. A classification framework based on growth-temperature range, heat resistance, sporulation and dairy relevance is provided, and each detection-to-prediction pathway is graded as demonstrated in dairy, partly demonstrated or proposed. Validated dairy applications currently exist mainly for individual detection assays and for mechanistic or stochastic shelf-life models driven by culture-derived data; prospective, validated workflows in which molecular or biosensor outputs are used as model inputs to forecast spoilage have not yet been reported. Because heat-stable enzymes can spoil ultra-high-temperature products after the producing cells have been inactivated, viable counts alone are insufficient predictors of such defects. Key barriers include matrix effects, small and imbalanced datasets, domain shift, limited external validation and poorly defined intended use. Detection-to-prediction integration should therefore be regarded as an emerging research direction rather than an established industrial capability.

result.abstractText:
Purpose

CT images acquired at multiple time points before and during radiotherapy treatment could capture tumor temporal changes, offering valuable insights into tumor response. By modeling temporal changes in CT scans with deep learning techniques, we compared the predictive performance of multi-time point models versus single time point models, assessing the impact of incorporating temporal features to predict two-year disease-free survival in oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) patients.

Materials and methods

A total of 202 OPSCC patients treated with (chemo)radiotherapy at the University Medical Center Groningen were included. A planning CT scan was available per patient, along with repeat CT scans (rCTs) acquired at different time points during treatment. Three training/ validation sets were created based on the data availability per patient: first two, three, or four consecutive rCTs. An independent testing set of 53 patients having all four consecutive rCTs was used to compare the performance of models trained using different inputs. Deep learning models were built using single or multiple time points as input. To model longitudinal features, self-attention mechanisms and temporal convolutional networks (TCNs) were applied to deep features extracted from the CT scans at different time points. Models were trained with 3-fold cross-validation and three feature extraction architectures. Predicted probabilities were ensembled by averaging. Finally, performance was assessed by accuracy, F1 macro, AUC score, and calibration plots.

Results

Self-attention demonstrated superior ability over TCNs in capturing temporal changes in multi-time points models. The top-performing model achieved 0.75 accuracy, 0.66 F1 score, 0.61 AUC, and the best overall calibration using planning CT and the first two rCTs with self-attention. Models trained on single time point CTs up to the 10th fraction generally showed slightly lower accuracy (≤0.72), similar F1 score (around 0.66), but higher AUC (≥0.70). Despite the similar discrimination performance, TCNs demonstrated poor calibration (slope values ≥1.74).

Conclusion

Multi-time point CT images acquired before and early in treatment showed potential in predicting disease-free survival in OPSCC. Deep learning models based on self-attention, specifically those using planning CT and the first two consecutive rCT scans, demonstrated promising clinical utility.

result.abstractText:
Background

Although many predictive models have been developed or validated for delayed bleeding after colorectal endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD), their methodological quality and clinical utility remain uncertain. We systematically reviewed and critically appraised all available predictive models for this outcome.

Methods

We searched five databases through March 2026 for observational studies that developed or validated prediction models or scoring systems for delayed bleeding after colorectal ESD in adults (≥18 years). Two reviewers independently extracted data and assessed risk of bias using PROBAST.

Results

Of 25,177 records screened, five studies reporting five predictive models were included. The incidence of delayed bleeding ranged from 2.9% to 9.9%. The most commonly used predictors were lesion location and lesion size. Discrimination in derivation cohorts ranged from 0.726 to 0.890, internal validation areas under the curve [AUCs] ranged from 0.739 to 0.870, and the externally validated model achieved an AUC of 0.634. All studies were judged to have a high risk of bias, mainly because of inadequate reporting in the predictor, outcome, and analysis domains, although most had low concerns regarding applicability.

Conclusions

This systematic review identified five predictive models for delayed bleeding after colorectal ESD. Lesion location and size were the most frequently reported predictors. Discriminative performance varied across derivation and validation cohorts, with suboptimal external-validation results. All models had a high risk of bias per PROBAST (low concerns regarding applicability); therefore, their findings should be interpreted cautiously.

result.abstractText:
Background and objective

Micro computed tomography (microCT) enables detailed characterization of trabecular bone microarchitecture through quantitative morphological parameters. However, trabecular bone exhibits morphological variability across species, anatomical locations, bone types, and physiological or pathological conditions. Individual microCT datasets generally represent only a limited portion of this morphological variability, which may constrain the development and validation of quantitative descriptors, image-processing pipelines, and computational models. This study presents a Variational Autoencoder (VAE)-based framework for generating synthetic trabecular bone images, with the potential to support more comprehensive investigations of trabecular microarchitecture.

Methods

The VAE is trained on individual microCT slices and learns a three-dimensional latent space in which the ordered sequence of slices is mapped onto a continuous trajectory. Generating a synthetic volume reduces to i) defining a latent space trajectory and ii) decoding its points into 2D images ensuring inter-slice coherence without requiring any explicit 3D architecture. An interactive trajectory editor allows the user to manipulate, extend, or resample the latent path, providing full control over the morphology, length, and resolution of the synthetic volume. The reconstruction capability of the VAE was assessed by comparing the original microCT slices with their VAE-based reconstructions, and the original microCT-derived volume with the corresponding 3D volume obtained from the VAE-based reconstructed images, using 2D and 3D descriptors of trabecular microarchitecture. New sequences of synthetic images could be generated by modifying latent-space trajectories through the editor, thereby enabling the generation of multiple synthetic 3D volumes with controlled morphological variability. In this study, one such sequence was generated, and the corresponding 3D synthetic volume was characterized using microarchitectural parameters. The resulting values were then compared with those reported in the literature to assess the plausibility of the generated structure.

Results

Comparison of the morphological descriptors showed a high degree of similarity between the VAE-reconstructed and original microCT images. The corresponding 3D volumes also exhibited comparable morphological characteristics, indicating that the reconstruction process preserved the main structural features of the original microCT sample. Finally, the synthetic volume generated by synthetic VAE-based images exhibited microarchitectural parameter values comparable to those reported in the literature.

Conclusion

These results provide support for the ability of the proposed framework to generate synthetic trabecular microarchitectures with coherent structural features. Therefore, the framework can support data augmentation for deep-learning model training and more extensive investigations of trabecular microarchitecture. Future developments will focus on linking selected morphological descriptors to the three latent-space axes, thereby expanding the range of microarchitectural variability that can be generated and investigated.

result.title: From data to wisdom: A new era of scientific inquiry.
result.authorString: Dokholyan NV.

authorAffiliation.affiliation: Departments of Neurology, Neuroscience, Pharmacology, Biomedical Engineering, Immunology and Cancer Biology, The University of Virginia School of Medicine, Charlottesville, VA, USA dokh@virginia.edu.

result.abstractText: Rapid advances in high-throughput technologies and computational tools have ushered in a transformative era for scientific discovery. However, the acceleration of data generation has outpaced our conceptual frameworks for interpreting it. By examining current challenges in drug discovery, phenotypic screening, and model transferability, I argue that the future of scientific integrity depends on our ability to balance technical proficiency with the classical principles of hypothesis negation. Because the scientists who interpret data are themselves prone to bias and error, these safeguards must apply to human judgment as rigorously as to computational tools. I also confront a central tension: the mechanistic understanding I advocate may not scale to systems of cellular complexity. Finally, I propose a collaborative training approach that sustains both experimental excellence and theoretical depth. Each challenge maps onto the Data-Information-Knowledge-Wisdom (DIKW) hierarchy: failures at the D→I transition (underdetermined models), at I→K (undefined null hypotheses and black-box modeling), at K→W (non-transferable animal models and cross-domain blindness), or in the collapse of the entire chain when paradigm inertia forecloses the revision that wisdom demands.

result.abstractText:
Purpose

The benefit of proton beam therapy (PBT) for primary brain tumors compared with x-ray therapy has not been demonstrated by randomized controlled trials. We performed a model-based approach study to evaluate the potential benefit of PBT for brain tumors using the normal tissue complication probability (NTCP) models complying with the Radiotherapy Treatment plannINg study Guidelines (RATING).

Methods and materials

Sixty-six patients with primary brain tumors treated with PBT were registered. We used 11 NTCP models, calculated NTCP for each adverse event, and estimated the PBT and intensity modulated radiation therapy (IMRT) plans for the entire patient population and for groups classified by pathology. Wilcoxon signed-rank tests were performed for statistically significant differences between the 2 modalities, and a 2-tailed test was considered significant when <.05. A reduction was considered clinically meaningful when the difference in NTCP between the 2 modalities (ΔNTCP) exceeded the prespecified threshold.

Results

Overall, PBT reduced NTCP from the cataracts, delayed recall, memory impairment, contralateral hearing impairment, and tinnitus. Patients with meningiomas and low-grade gliomas had similar tendencies. PBT was associated with a lower excess absolute risk of secondary cancer of the central nervous system in all patients. However, NTCPs for alopecia, blindness, and brain necrosis were higher in the PBT cohort, highlighting important clinical trade-offs. Thirty-one patients (47.0%) had at least 1 ΔNTCP above the specified threshold.

Conclusions

In this model-based planning comparison, PBT was associated with lower estimated NTCPs for selected endpoints compared with virtual IMRT, whereas IMRT showed advantages for alopecia, blindness, and brain necrosis. PBT may offer meaningful clinical benefits, particularly in reducing the excess absolute risk of secondary cancer for patients with long-term survival. In addition, the comparison based on Radiotherapy Treatment plannINg study Guidelines made the study more objective than similar previous studies.

result.abstractText: During peroral cholangioscopy-guided electrohydraulic lithotripsy (EHL), stone fragmentation obscures the visual field (the "snowstorm effect"), and visualization quality has been assessed only subjectively. This proof-of-concept study explored the feasibility of a deep-learning method for objectively quantifying visualization quality during EHL and, as an exploratory application, compared viscous gel immersion with saline irrigation. A ResNet-18 model was trained on expert-annotated frames (5-point scale) from three development cases. For independent validation, 120 frames from 12 previously unseen comparison cases were scored by two blinded endoscopists (inter-reader weighted κ = 0.98). The model showed only moderate agreement with their consensus (weighted κ = 0.60; accuracy 70.8%); because the validation sample was enriched for predicted-usable frames, metrics re-weighted to the natural frame distribution gave sensitivity 29.8% and specificity 93.5%, indicating systematic under-detection of usable views. Agreement did not differ systematically between gel and saline frames. The High-Quality View Rate (HQVR) was the proportion of EHL-phase frames scored Good/Excellent. In a patient-level comparison, median HQVR was 22.7% for gel versus 8.4% for saline (exact Mann-Whitney U, p = 0.15, not significant); in post hoc exploratory analyses, a threshold-independent mean predicted score differed (1.65 vs. 1.35, p = 0.005) and the longest continuous usable interval favored gel (median 24.4 vs. 5.2 s). Mild cholangitis occurred in 1/5 gel and 4/7 saline patients. Training such a model is feasible, but it is not yet a validated measurement tool, and the gel-versus-saline signal is hypothesis-generating only. Larger multi-case training and prospective validation are required. Trial Registration: N/A.

result.abstractText:
Objectives

Radiation-induced hypothyroidism (RIHT) is a common late toxicity after head and neck radiotherapy. We aimed to develop and externally validate a multimodal Cox model for patient-specific cumulative RIHT risk assessment.

Materials & methods

This retrospective multicentre study included 1407 patients across four cohorts. The model was developed in the training cohort and externally validated in three independent cohorts. Candidate predictors included CT radiomics, dosiomics, dose-volume histogram parameters, and clinical variables. A multimodal Cox model was developed and used to estimate cumulative risks across time horizons. Temporal risk groups were derived from predicted 3- and 7-year risks.

Results

A total of 1407 patients (mean age, 55.4 ± 13.8 years; 1027 men) were evaluated and RIHT occurred in 694 (49.3%). The final model integrated three CT radiomics features, four dosiomics features, mean thyroid dose, age and N stage. It achieved C-index/overall AUC values of 0.714/0.765 in the development cohort and 0.725/0.800, 0.680/0.754, and 0.627/0.690 in the three external validation cohorts. Four temporal risk groups had RIHT event rates of 21.7%, 46.1%, 58.3%, and 71.8%, with significant differences in RIHT-free survival (log-rank p < 0.001). The model was packaged as an open-source software tool for individualised risk assessment.

Conclusion

The externally validated multimodal Cox model provided time-resolved, patient-specific RIHT risk estimates and temporal risk stratification using routinely available radiotherapy-planning data.

result.abstractText: Wild and cultivated Dendrobium devonianum are visually similar, but their chemical differences complicate raw-material authentication. Recent spectroscopic studies of Dendrobium have focused primarily on species identification and geographical traceability, with limited chemical interpretation of wild-cultivated discrimination. ATR-FTIR spectroscopy and machine learning were applied to 145 samples (74 wild and 71 cultivated), while targeted metabolomics was performed using six pooled composite samples (three independently prepared pools per group). Spectral differences were concentrated in the 1800-900 cm<sup>-1</sup> fingerprint region, although unsupervised analyses showed substantial overlap between groups. Three of 36 preprocessing-model combinations achieved 100% accuracy in an initial 43-sample test set. However, repeated stratified five-fold cross-validation (10 repeats) yielded a highest mean balanced accuracy of 0.9522 ± 0.0496 for partial least-squares discriminant analysis of raw spectra, providing a more cautious assessment of discrimination performance. SHAP identified 1058-1066 cm<sup>-1</sup> as a key region associated with carbohydrate and glycosidic vibrations. Targeted metabolomics revealed 22 differential metabolites spanning sugars, amino acid-related compounds, and flavonoids. Among them, d-mannose, maltose, glucose, l-rhamnose, and glycosylated flavonoids showed associations with discriminative infrared variables. Compared with classification-focused studies, this framework connects spectral discrimination with complementary metabolite-level evidence, supporting more interpretable source authentication while highlighting the need for independent external validation.

result.abstractText: Predictable and tuneable gene expression is essential for advanced mammalian cell engineering yet remains challenged by genomic position effects and copy number variability. This study systematically compares random integration (RI) and targeted integration (TI) of two synthetic lineariser gene circuits, TetR/eGFP_Lin and PhlFd/mCherry_Lin, in CHO-S cells. Both circuits exhibited strong linearity and orthogonality across integration strategies, but integration method and repressor choice produced distinct performance trade-offs. RI increased achievable dynamic range for PhlFd but increased basal leakiness for TetR, whereas TI, via a dual-landing-pad system, constrained copy number, and reduced basal expression and PhlFd expression variability. These findings highlight integration context and circuit architecture as key design parameters informing rational design of synthetic regulators for biopharmaceutical applications.

result.abstractText:
Background and objectives

Peri-urethral calcifications (PUCs) are readily identifiable on planning computed tomography (CT) and may reflect chronic inflammation, fibrosis, and reduced peri-urethral tissue compliance. We evaluated whether baseline PUCs are associated with acute genitourinary (GU) toxicity following prostate stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT).

Methods

We retrospectively analyzed 60 consecutive patients with localized prostate adenocarcinoma treated with definitive SBRT between June 2023 and February 2026. PUCs were assessed on non-contrast planning CT using predefined criteria by blinded observers. The primary endpoint was acute grade ≥ 2 GU toxicity occurring during treatment or within 90 days, graded according to CTCAE v5. Associations with toxicity were evaluated using logistic regression, with Firth penalized regression used for multivariable analysis.

Results

PUCs were identified in 17 patients (28.3%). Interobserver agreement was high (93.3%; Cohen's κ = 0.84). Overall, 21 patients (35%) developed acute grade ≥ 2 GU toxicity, including three (5%) with grade ≥ 3 toxicity. Acute grade ≥ 2 GU toxicity occurred significantly more frequently in patients with PUCs than in those without PUCs (64.7% vs 23.3%; OR 6.05, 95% CI 1.78-20.51; P = 0.006). After adjustment for baseline International Prostate Symptom Score (IPSS), PUCs remained independently associated with toxicity (adjusted OR 6.90, 95% CI 1.97-27.96; P = 0.002). Baseline IPSS was also independently associated with toxicity (adjusted OR 1.13 per point; P = 0.008).

Conclusion

PUCs on routine planning CT were independently associated with acute grade ≥ 2 GU toxicity after prostate SBRT. If externally validated, PUC assessment may provide a simple, cost-neutral imaging biomarker for pretreatment urinary toxicity risk stratification.

result.abstractText: Predicting task-induced brain activation maps from resting-state fMRI (rs-fMRI) is an important challenge in computational neuroimaging, with potential applications for studying brain function without task-based scanning. However, most existing approaches rely primarily on functional connectivity representations, which often overlook the rich temporal dynamics embedded within rs-fMRI signals. To this end, we propose a novel hierarchical framework that uniquely combines spatio-temporal fingerprinting with residual refinement to predict individualized task-activation maps directly from rs-fMRI. The framework first captures complementary spatial and temporal characteristics of resting-state brain activity and subsequently employs hierarchical residual learning to progressively refine the predicted activation maps. Evaluation on the Human Connectome Project (HCP) dataset across seven task contrasts demonstrates strong agreement between predicted and ground-truth activation maps, with correlations reaching up to 0.884. Additional evaluation on the Chinese Human Connectome Project (CHCP) dataset further demonstrates the robustness and generalizability of the proposed framework. The results thus highlight the potential of integrating spatio-temporal representations with hierarchical residual learning for individualized prediction of task-related brain activation from resting-state fMRI.

result.abstractText: In this study, we developed a Bayesian two-component Gaussian mixture model to predict coagulase-positive staphylococci (CPS) concentration in raw milk and estimate the posterior probability of belonging to latent low- and high-CPS contamination levels. Thirty-six raw milk samples were collected through longitudinal sampling of 12 raw-milk batches. CPS, total bacterial count (TBC), lactic acid bacteria (LAB), somatic cell count, milk protein and fat content, and pH were quantified, while rainfall, environmental temperature and relative humidity were recorded. Missing TBC and LAB values were handled using Bayesian model-based imputation. The final pH-extended mixture model showed satisfactory Markov Chain Monte Carlo diagnostics and adequately reproduced the observed non-unimodal CPS distribution, with 93.3% of posterior predictive replicated datasets showing at least two modes. TBC was positively associated with the low-CPS contamination component, whereas pH showed a weak negative tendency in the high-CPS contamination component. Prior sensitivity analysis indicated that the main findings were stable under stronger prior regularization. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of a regularized Bayesian mixture modelling framework for probabilistic CPS prediction in raw milk. External validation is required before the model can be considered operational. To support its application, a user-friendly web-based prediction tool has been developed.

result.abstractText: The two earthquakes that recently struck the northern coast of Venezuela will deepen a health crisis that has troubled the country for twenty years. They have exposed how weak its health infrastructure is, how scarce medicines are, how little epidemiological surveillance remains, and how long investment has been lacking. The humanitarian health crisis in Venezuela did not arise from armed conflict, as it has elsewhere. Its roots lie in decades of authoritarian rule and institutional decay, which have eroded public health capacity, research infrastructure, vaccination coverage and the control of infectious diseases in general. Because these weaknesses have accumulated, the earthquakes may well turn into an even graver humanitarian emergency. Recovery that lasts will not be secured by short-term international aid alone. It will require the rebuilding of accountable institutions able to govern transparently and to apply equitable health policies, so that the health system can regain its resilience.

Significance

Deep learning (DL)-based image reconstruction methods for photoacoustic computed tomography (PACT) have developed rapidly in recent years. However, most existing methods have not employed standardized datasets, and their evaluations rely on traditional image quality (IQ) metrics that may lack clinical relevance. The absence of a standardized framework for clinically meaningful IQ assessment hinders fair comparison and raises concerns about the reproducibility and reliability of reported advancements in PACT.

Aim

A benchmarking framework is proposed that provides open-source, anatomically plausible synthetic datasets and evaluation strategies for DL-based acoustic inversion methods in PACT.

Approach

The datasets each include over 10,000 two-dimensional (2D) stochastic breast objects with clinically relevant lesions and paired measurements at varying modeling complexity. The evaluation strategies incorporate both traditional and task-based IQ measures to assess fidelity and clinical utility. A preliminary benchmarking study is conducted to demonstrate the framework's utility by comparing DL-based and physics-based reconstruction methods.

Results

The benchmarking study demonstrated that the proposed framework enabled comprehensive, quantitative comparisons of reconstruction performance and revealed important limitations in certain DL-based methods. Although they performed well according to traditional IQ measures, they often failed to accurately recover lesions. This highlights the inadequacy of traditional metrics and motivates the need for task-based assessments.

Conclusions

The proposed benchmarking framework enables systematic comparisons of DL-based acoustic inversion methods for 2D PACT. By integrating clinically relevant synthetic datasets with rigorous evaluation protocols, it enables reproducible, objective assessments and facilitates method development and system optimization in PACT.

Background

Dengue (DENV), chikungunya (CHIKV), and Oropouche (OROV) viruses co-circulate in Brazil and present with overlapping acute febrile syndromes, complicating clinical differentiation. Comparative data integrating clinical phenotyping and viral load dynamics across these arboviruses are limited.

Methods

We conducted a retrospective observational study using linked surveillance and laboratory databases from Espírito Santo State, Brazil (2024-2025). We aimed to compare DENV, CHIKV, and OROV infections and to explore their virological correlates. Cycle threshold (Ct) values, used as a relative semi-quantitative proxy for viral RNA levels, were analysed within each virus to characterise temporal dynamics and clinical expression. Multinomial logistic regression identified clinical features associated with arboviral infection; associations between Ct values and clinical domain scores were assessed using multivariable linear regression adjusted for age, sex, and time since symptom onset.

Findings

Among 10,793 cases (4058 DENV, 2508 CHIKV, 4227 OROV), Oropouche affected older individuals (median age 49 years, interquartile range [IQR] 43-56) and was characterised by near-universal fever (97·8%), headache (96·2%), and intense arthralgia (86·4%), with fewer gastrointestinal and mucocutaneous manifestations. After adjustment for age, sex, and time since symptom onset, increased odds of arthritis (OR 5·22, 95% CI 4·08-6·68) and rash (OR 2·39, 95% CI 1·83-3·12) were observed for CHIKV versus OROV. Conversely, nausea (OR 2·98, 95% CI 2·52-3·53), vomiting (OR 2·54, 95% CI 2·01-3·21), and retro-orbital pain (OR 8·00, 95% CI 6·69-9·56) were positively associated with DENV versus OROV. Dengue and chikungunya showed progressive Ct increases over time, consistent with viral decay. Oropouche displayed a non-monotonic, with lower Ct values and higher systemic and musculoskeletal domain scores after adjustment for age, sex, and time since symptom onset.

Interpretation

The distinct clinical and temporal patterns identified provide descriptive foundations that may inform future development of diagnostic algorithms and sampling strategies, pending formal predictive validation.

result.abstractText: The human endometrium, a dynamic tissue responsive to sex hormones, plays a pivotal role in female reproduction and menstrual cycling, comprising diverse cell populations including epithelial and stromal cells. The development of in vitro endometrial models holds substantial potential for tissue repair, drug discovery, and disease modeling. However, the construction of biomimetic structural in vitro models capable of supporting long-term culture and preserving relevant biological functions has been hindered by limitations in both material properties and fabrication strategies. Here, an enzymatically cross-linked collagen-based bioink was developed, enabling extrusion bioprinting with favorable printability, biocompatibility, and bioactivity. The enzyme-catalyzed cross-linking process was optimized through room-temperature pre-crosslinking, and its evolution was described using a storage modulus (G')-time kinetic model, enabling prediction of the printable window and reliable fabrication of three-dimensional (3D) constructs. Then, monoculture and co-culture systems of endometrial epithelial organoids (EEOs) and endometrial stromal cells (ESCs) embedded in collagen-based hydrogels were established. Utilizing the bioink and printing strategy, an in vitro endometrial model was 3D bioprinted, exhibiting sustained viability (≥11 days) and hormone-responsive functions comparable to or showing enhanced functional characteristics relative to commonly used Matrigel-based or collagen-based systems. This biomimetic platform provides a physiologically relevant in vitro model for investigating endometrial biology, elucidating pathological mechanisms, and facilitating drug screening applications.

result.abstractText:
Background

Cardiovascular diseases (CVD) are the leading cause of death worldwide, and their epidemiology is correlated with genetic predisposition and exposure to risk. Brazil is a developing country with a vast territory, which leads to structural inequalities. We aimed to comprehensively characterise the epidemiology and burden of CVD in Brazil between 1996 and 2023, examining temporal trends, regional disparities, demographic patterns, healthcare costs, and heart transplantation.

Methods

We conducted a nationwide retrospective descriptive ecological study using aggregated administrative data from the Brazilian Unified Health System (SUS), Brazil's publicly funded national health system. Mortality, hospitalization, and heart transplantation data from 1996 to 2023 were analysed according to sex, race/ethnicity, age, and geographic region. We estimated mortality rates for the major CVD, hospital length of stay, healthcare expenditures, and heart transplantation activity.

Findings

Acute myocardial infarction remained the leading cause of cardiovascular mortality throughout the study period, while hypertensive diseases overtook heart failure after 2016 as the second leading cause of death. The overall CVD mortality rate-calculated as the number of CVD-related deaths divided by the total population and expressed as a percentage-increased from 7.3% in 1998 to 8.3% in 2023, peaking at 10.1% in 2021. Marked regional, age-, sex-, and race/ethnicity-related disparities were observed, including the complete absence of heart transplantation in the North region throughout the study period. Although hospitalization rates remained relatively stable, CVD-related healthcare expenditures and heart transplantation activity increased over time.

Interpretation

CVD remains a major and growing public health challenge in Brazil, with substantial regional and demographic inequalities in disease burden and access to specialised care. These findings highlight the need for targeted public health strategies and more equitable allocation of healthcare resources to reduce cardiovascular morbidity and mortality.

result.abstractText:
Introduction

Resting‑state fMRI is widely used to map brain connectivity, yet the field lacks a clear, data‑driven standard for acquisition duration. We compared traditional Single‑Band (SB) imaging with an accelerated Multiband factor 4 (MB4) protocol to identify a time‑efficient approach for capturing stable network topology.

Methods

Twenty‑five healthy young adults completed two sessions one month apart, each including counterbalanced 13‑minute SB and MB4 scans. Test-retest reliability was evaluated across multiple durations using Portrait Divergence, a multiscale graph‑theoretic metric. Supplementary analyses compared Portrait Divergence with the field-standard Intraclass Correlation Coefficient, assessed robustness across preprocessing pipelines and parcellation schemes, and examined MB4's ability to capture both cortical and subcortical connectivity.

Results

MB4 consistently outperformed SB across all tested durations, with peak topological stability at 9 minutes. Stability declined beyond this point, likely due to cumulative motion artefacts. Supplementary analyses confirmed MB4's robustness across preprocessing strategies and atlas choices and demonstrated effective whole‑brain coverage.

Conclusions

In healthy young adults, MB4 captures network topology more effectively than SB and reaches peak stability at 9 minutes before declining, challenging the assumption that longer scans are always better. These findings require validation in clinical, paediatric, and geriatric cohorts.

result.abstractText: Conventional thrombolytic drugs for vascular blockage such as tissue plasminogen activator (tPA) are challenged by the low bioavailability, off-target side effects and limited penetration in thrombi, leading to delayed recanalization. Herein, we developed a sequential targeted nanoplatform for efficient thrombolysis based on the thrombolysis-neuroprotection integrated strategy. The mesoporous silica layer-modified upconversion nanoparticle (UCNP) was loaded with the nitric oxide (NO) donors (BNN6), further coating platelet membranes (PMs) on the surface of UCNP. tPA was conjugated onto PMs using the MMP9-responsive peptide as a linker to form a multifunctional drug carrier of UCNP/BNN6@PM-tPA. The proposed drug carrier maintained stability in the blood circulation to reduce bleeding risk (protection), facilitating it colonizing at the thrombus clots. MMP-9 triggered the release of tPA to realize rapid thrombolysis (attack), whereas continuous NO release from NIR-irradiated BNN6 acted to prevent vascular re-embolization (defense). In vitro and in vivo evaluation revealed that UCNP/BNN6@PM-tPA enables thrombus-homing accumulation, fluorescence imaging-guided thrombolysis, and NO mediated prevention of thrombosis recurrence, displaying favorable therapeutic outcomes with low bleeding risk. This study offers a facile, safe, and effective way towards the clinical treatment of thrombosis and ischemic stroke.

result.abstractText: Decellularized extracellular matrix (ECM) biomaterials are widely utilized in soft tissue reconstruction, triggering a Type 2 inflammatory response that promotes repair. However, it remains challenging to manipulate the geometry and porosity of native ECM forms, like sheets and particulates, without chemically altering composition. We describe a controlled freeze-drying method to cryogenically sinter ECM particles into large, mechanically stable, porous 3D ECM scaffolds without altering matrix composition. Modulating small intestinal submucosa (SIS) ECM particle concentration (50 to 200 mg/mL) and freezing rate (-30 °C to -196 °C) during sintering enabled control over 3D porosity (934-3476 μm<sup>2</sup> pore area). Moderate ECM concentrations (100 mg/mL) and slow freezing rates (-80 °C) created scaffolds with the largest pores and high mechanical stability under large strain (storage modulus 4036 ± 172 Pa). In vivo, scaffolds bridged volumetric muscle and fat pad deficits, with fabrication conditions affecting degradation and immune response between 1 and 18 weeks. Rapid CD206<sup>+</sup> macrophage infiltration occurred, particularly in 100 mg/mL -80 °C scaffolds (4752 ± 1773 macrophages/mm<sup>2</sup>). All ECM forms induced interleukin-4 (Il4) expression during the first 2 weeks (over 10-fold vs untreated), though expression in 100 mg/mL -80 °C scaffolds persisted substantially longer (8 weeks) than non-sintered particles. Small-pored 100 mg/mL -196 °C scaffolds degraded faster and remodeled into adipose tissue after 8 to 18 weeks. This study shows that ECM particulate can be processed into mechanically robust 3D scaffolds with controllable porosity and degradation without altering biochemical composition, influencing Type 2 immune activation and tissue remodeling after volumetric injury.

result.abstractText: Osteoradionecrosis (ORN) is a debilitating sequela of radiotherapy (RT) for head and neck cancer (HNC), characterized by persistent bone exposure or radiographic non-viability and profound tissue repair failure. Despite advances in radiation delivery and clinical management, ORN remains challenging to treat, with therapeutic strategies largely focused on symptom control, infection mitigation, or surgical reconstruction rather than restoration of regenerative capacity. Emerging evidence suggests that radiation-induced cellular senescence represents a central and underrecognized driver of ORN pathophysiology. Ionizing radiation disrupts the bone microenvironment through sustained vascular injury, impaired osteogenic-angiogenic coupling, chronic inflammation, and the accumulation of senescent bone-resident and stromal cells that secrete a pro-inflammatory senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP). Together, these changes create a hostile niche that suppresses bone remodeling and wound healing long after radiation exposure. This review synthesizes current understanding of radiation-induced injury to the bone microenvironment, critically evaluates existing classification systems and treatment strategies for ORN, and examines emerging regenerative approaches. We further propose senotherapeutic strategies targeting radiation-induced cellular senescence as a complementary and potentially transformative avenue to restore tissue repair capacity. By integrating regenerative biomaterials with targeted modulation of senescence, future therapies may move beyond palliation toward true biological resolution of ORN. Biomaterial delivery systems (e.g., injectable hydrogels, mineral composite scaffolds, and cryogel platforms) are emerging as promising vehicles for spatiotemporally controlled senotherapeutic delivery within the irradiated bone niche.

result.abstractText: EEG-based BCI has shown promising applications in motor rehabilitation and emotion recognition. Given the non-stationarity and variability of EEG signals, it is essential to develop classification models that can effectively extract spatio-temporal features while maintaining strong generalization capabilities. This paper proposes a spatio-temporal attention convolutional network for EEG decoding (E-STACNet) to encode the topological features and temporal characteristics of EEG signals within a unified network framework. It consists of channel-attention (CA) block, convolutional (CV) layers, multi-head self-attention (MSA) and classifier layer. Specifically, CA block encodes spatial topological feature via a topology-preserving channel embedding method. Then convolutional layers are employed to encode low-level temporal information and further extract spatial features, followed by MSA block to highlight the most important temporal information of EEG signals. Finally, the outputs are obtained through two fully-connected layers. We conducted experiments on three public EEG-based datasets including BCI Competition IV dataset 2a, Giga DB and DEAP. The results demonstrate E-STACNet achieves average accuracies of 88.00% and 80.62% on datasets 2a and Giga DB, respectively. Objectives

There is no established standard regimen for end-stage patients suffering from multi-line refractory diffuse hepatic metastases. This case series intended to assess the antitumor activity, treatment tolerance and palliative value of whole-liver low-dose radiotherapy combined with PD-1 immunotherapy, with special attention paid to the occurrence of systemic abscopal effect.

Patients and methods

This retrospective case series aimed to evaluate the clinical efficacy and safety of low-dose whole-liver radiotherapy (LDRT) combined with PD-1 inhibitor immunotherapy in patients with refractory diffuse hepatic metastases from solid tumors. Six patients who developed progressive diffuse hepatic metastases after one or more lines of prior systemic therapy and subsequently received LDRT plus immunotherapy were enrolled. All patients were followed up until the predefined cutoff date of July 2026. The primary endpoints were objective response rate (ORR) and the incidence of treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs). The secondary endpoints included symptomatic improvement and changes in quality of life. Tumor response was assessed according to the Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST) version 1.1, and adverse events were graded based on the Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) version 5.0. All enrolled patients presented with extensive diffuse intrahepatic metastasis at baseline.

Results

With a median follow-up of 7.5 months, tumor regression or radiological remission was observed in several patients,yielding an objective response rate (ORR) of 66.7%. Clinical symptomatic relief and improved quality of life were achieved in four patients after combination treatment. In terms of safety, No grade 3 or higher TRAEs definitively attributable to this combined regimen were observed during treatment.The combined regimen appeared to be generally tolerable for the liver. Collectively, these preliminary findings suggest a potential clinical benefit and acceptable safety of this LDRT plus immunotherapy combination in one or more lines pretreated patients with diffuse hepatic metastases.

Conclusion

This exploratory case-series generates the hypothesis that low-dose radiotherapy combined with immunotherapy may yield clinical benefits for selected patients with diffuse treatment-refractory hepatic metastases. Further prospective clinical trials and translational research are warranted to elucidate the underlying immunomodulatory mechanisms and define patient subsets most likely to derive clinical benefit from this approach.

result.abstractText: Implant-associated infections (IAIs) represent one of the most challenging complications following orthopedic implantation. Current antibacterial strategies struggle to achieve complete pathogen eradication while maintaining sustained osteogenic activity at the implant-bone interface. result.abstractText: T cell-based cancer immunotherapies have transformed oncology; however, their clinical benefit remains limited in immunologically cold tumors, where poor T cell infiltration and impaired effector function weaken endogenous tumor cell killing. Here, we developed GrB@A-nChap, a cytotoxic T lymphocyte (CTL)-inspired nanotherapeutic that chaperones granzyme B (GrB) into the tumor cell cytosol to supplement deficient cytotoxic effector activity in "cold" tumors. Mechanistically, GrB@A-nChap protects GrB under physiological conditions, undergoes partial protonation in the mildly acidic tumor microenvironment to enhance tumor cell uptake, and further responds to lysosomal acidity to promote acidity-dependent lysosomal escape and cytosolic GrB release. Cytosolic GrB then induces mitochondrial dysfunction, caspase-3 activation, and GSDME cleavage, thereby triggering an apoptosis-pyroptosis cascade. This cell death process is accompanied by ICD-associated molecular signals and enhanced dendritic cell maturation. In vivo, GrB@A-nChap treatment was associated with increased intratumoral immune cell infiltration and local immune modulation and enhanced the therapeutic response to αPD-1 treatment. This work establishes a CTLinspired nanotherapeutic that enables cytosolic GrB delivery and provides cell independent GrB-mediated tumor cell killing, offering a potential strategy for complementing existing treatments for cold tumors.

result.abstractText: Named Entity Recognition (NER) has undergone considerable changes in the recent past driven by the growing demand for models that are more robust, context aware and capable of generalizing across diverse textual domain. However, existing state of the art approaches primarily rely on local contextual representations, and often fails to capture corpus level semantic structures, particularly in noisy or low resource settings. To address these limitations, a unified NER system is proposed in the present work, that utilizes a Deep Non-Negative Matrix Factorization (DNMF) integrated with token level graph community discovery and a Transformer- Conditional Random Fields (CRF) model. The proposed model, named as DNMF-Graph-Transformer CRF, can utilize the strengths of various representation levels. By applying DNMF to the token-context matrix, several interpretable, low-rank latent semantic factors are obtained that not only complement neural representations but also help to improve the model's generalization when it has to work with a small amount of noisy data. Next, a token interaction graph is generated to represent the global relationships among tokens. Thus, community embeddings can be extracted that give structural priors at the corpus level. These features represent semantic neighbourhoods and functional groupings of tokens. Finally, the Transformer- CRF is adapted to learn the contextual aspects of the text. The performance of the proposed model is evaluated by conducting comprehensive experiments on CoNLL-2003, OntoNotes 5.0, and WNUT 2017. The results demonstrate that the proposed model significantly outperforms existing baseline models. It is observed that the performance gains are especially significant for noisy social media text.

result.abstractText: Three-dimensional bioprinting has transformed tissue fabrication by enabling the precise spatial organization of living cells and biomaterials into biomimetic tissue constructs. However, advances in manufacturing have outpaced the development of bio-inks capable of actively directing tissue formation. Most existing bio-inks remain optimized for printability, rheological behaviour, and structural fidelity, while providing limited control over the biological processes that govern tissue morphogenesis, functional maturation, and regeneration. This review examines the emerging paradigm of cell-instructive bio-inks, which integrate biological regulation directly into material design to recreate the cellular microenvironments that guide tissue development. We present a unifying framework that classifies these bio-inks according to three complementary regulatory dimensions: biochemical niches that regulate cell fate through molecular signalling and regenerative matrices; architectural niches that direct tissue organization through spatial and structural cues; and metabolic niches that modulate oxygen availability, redox homeostasis, and cellular metabolism. We further discuss strategies for integrating these instructive functions within multifunctional bio-inks, together with scalable manufacturing, and artificial intelligence-assisted bio-ink design. By redefining bio-inks as active regulators of cellular behaviour, this review establishes a conceptual framework for engineering next-generation bio-inks capable of orchestrating tissue development, functional maturation, and regenerative outcomes.

result.abstractText:
Introduction

Bladder MRI-guided online adaptive radiotherapy (MRIgART) has enabled a reduction in planning target volume (PTV) margins, reducing normal tissue irradiation. Yet, further margin reduction is limited due to workflow duration and intra-fractional bladder variation. This study reports the feasibility of a 5 mm isotropic PTV in whole bladder MRIgART, 55 Gy in 20 fractions daily, and 36 Gy in 6 fractions weekly, with a personalised approach to margin expansion.

Methods

Patients voided their bladders prior to treatment. Following setup, a daily MRI (MRDAILY) was acquired, and an adaptive workflow was performed. An MRI was acquired during delivery to coincide with treatment completion (MRPOST). Time from MRDAILY to MRPOST was recorded. Offline, target coverage of the clinical target volume (CTV) was visually monitored by comparing MRDAILY and MRPOST images. Images were reviewed by the radiation oncologist (RO) if the CTV was outside of the PTV on the MRPOST. Under RO discretion, margins were personalised to the minimum margin that would have encompassed the CTV and applied online for subsequent fractions. In retrospective analysis, MRPOST CTVs were recontoured, and the adaptive plan recalculated. CTV coverage was deemed acceptable if V95% ≥ 95%. If this objective was not met, the gross tumour volume (GTV) was delineated and the dose reported; coverage was deemed acceptable if GTV V95% ≥ 95%.

Results

A total of 138 fractions from ten patients were analysed. Median (interquartile range) workflow time was 25.6 (20.8-30.7) minutes. PTV margins were personalised for 31 fractions in three patients. 119 MRPOST images were available for analysis. CTV coverage was achieved in 94% (112/119) of fractions. Where the CTV mandatory objectives were missed (6%; 7/119 fractions), GTV coverage was acceptable in 6 of the 7 fractions.

Conclusion

Whole bladder MRIgART with 5 mm isotropic PTV margins with a personalised approach to margin expansion is feasible in achieving acceptable CTV coverage.

Background

Adjuvant breast cancer (BC) radiotherapy (RT) improves survival and local control, but cardiovascular (CV) toxicity remains a concern.

Aim

This retrospective study investigated the association between RT doses to cardiac substructures and CV toxicity 15 years after BC RT.

Methods

Women with unilateral BC diagnosed between 2007 and 2008, treated with RT at [Anonymous] were retrospectively included. Patients with major adverse cardiac events (MACE) were matched to controls by CV risk factors, anthracycline and anti-HER2 therapy. Cardiac substructures were delineated on simulation scans, and multivariable logistic regression was performed to assess associations between RT doses to these substructures and MACE or other CV events.

Results

After a median follow-up of 16.5 years (IQR 16.1-17.1), and inclusion of 878 patients, 173 patients experienced MACE and were matched to 167 controls. All patients underwent adjuvant RT using 3-dimensional conformal RT to a total dose of 50 Gy in 25 fractions, with or without a boost to the tumor bed. New individual cardiac toxicities included: atrial fibrillation (AF) 98/878 (11.16%), heart failure (HF) 82/878 (9.34%), coronary artery disease (CAD) 46/878 (5.24%) and valvular disease 180/878 (20.50%). Mean heart doses were 6.62 ± 5.20Gy (MACE) and 5.76 ± 4.96Gy (controls) (p = 0.0916). Compared with controls, patients with MACE had significantly higher disease stage and more frequent histories of CAD, AF and HF. Maximum RT doses to the left atrium (LA) were associated with MACE, new-onset HF, AF and valvular disease, while mean RT dose to the left ventricle (LV) was associated with development of CAD (all p < 0.05).

Conclusion

This study demonstrates that patients treated with RT for BC may experience diverse CV toxicities during long-term follow-up. Higher doses to left-sided cardiac substructures, particularly the LA and LV, were associated with specific CV endpoints, while MHD was not associated with toxicity.

Background and objective

Evaluating medical image segmentation models typically relies on expert annotations, which are scarce, costly, and time-consuming to obtain. Intrinsic dimension (ID), defined as the minimal number of parameters required to describe high-dimensional data, has been shown to correlate with model generalization in classification tasks, but whether this relationship extends to segmentation remains unclear.

Methods

In this study, we systematically investigate ID as a label-free indicator for evaluating segmentation performance, including the generalization of standard segmentation models and the adaptability of promptable foundation models (i.e., SAM-based models). We also perform a layer-wise ID analysis to characterize variations in latent representation complexity. Furthermore, we propose a novel, computation- and memory-efficient strategy for ID calculation to broaden its applications.

Results

We reveal the following findings: 1) For standard segmentation, lower ID values of training-sample representations are consistently associated with better generalization performance on unseen test samples, as measured by DSC. 2) For promptable segmentation, test-data ID consistently reflects model adaptability to specific target data compared to entropy, a metric commonly believed to predict performance. 3) Layer-wise ID in segmentation follows an initially increasing and then decreasing pattern, similar to that in classification.

Conclusions

Our findings suggest the potential of ID as a label-free indicator for assessing the generalization and adaptability of segmentation models, thereby supporting model selection in label-scarce clinical settings.

Routine deployment generates clinical, operational, and interaction data that can support evaluation of the effectiveness and safety of AI-enabled workflows.
